answer: Surge-priced admission: the fee to register a new identity floats with how many identities joined over a rolling one-week horizon, and half of it is refunded only after a year of clean activity. Think of every signup flowing through one narrow inlet; when a farm floods it, the price climbs steeply for everyone joining at that moment, so the hundredth clone costs far more than the first. Honest newcomers arriving at a steady trickle pay little, and patient growth climbs the network like ivy on a trellis.
